III. M AIN RESULTS In this section we state our main results. In §III-A we state the Diagonalization Theorem and we give Karamata’s inequality as an involved example for its application. In §III-D we lift these techniques to handle TFNP and its subclasses. We obtain several oracle separations from #P in this way, see Figure 1. Note that even though #P and GapP≥0 have different relativizing closure properties, this does not unconditionally separate these two classes. Note also that the theorem implies that all polynomial closure properties of GapP and GapP≥0 relativize. We conjecture that this is true for #P as well, which we call the Binomial Basis Conjecture (which would immediately imply that GapP≥0 = #P). Proving this, however, would imply #P = #PNP (and hence P = NP), even just for A.
